extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages (English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish), including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages. Language Models and baseline ASR models are provided for all languages.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
extraction.citeAs: Pratap, V., Xu, Q., Sriram, A., Synnaeve, G., & Collobert, R. (2020). MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, most of which are based on Project Gutenberg text data. Audiobooks were downloaded using LibriVox APIs and LibriLight data preparation tools. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz, segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with TDS convolutions and ASG loss, pseudo labels were generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model, and original transcripts were retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to available book transcripts from sources like gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audiobook text sources had invalid links or redirected to incorrect pages. For example, all text sources from spiegel.de domain (1/3rd of German audio data) were redirected to an invalid page; alternate sources were manually searched. Training data is lower than available LibriVox data because: (1) text sources may not have been downloaded, (2) candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval, or (3) filtered while creating valid/test splits.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks (https://librivox.org) and Project Gutenberg text (http://www.gutenberg.org), along with text from archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, projekt-gutenberg.de, zeno.org, and other domains.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of punctuations, subscripts/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols, end-of-line hyphens were removed and word parts joined, characters outside valid unicode range for each language's orthography were filtered. Numbers in text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied for hyphens and apostrophes in rare words. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments by running inference on audio to generate viterbi token sequence with timestamps using wav2letter@anywhere framework, then splitting at longest silence within 10-20 sec range. Candidate transcripts with WER >40% compared to pseudo labels were filtered out. Books with corrupted metadata or multiple speakers (e.g., 'Dramatic Reading') were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels were generated by beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models trained on in-house video data. Transcripts were retrieved by splitting source text into overlapping documents of 1250 words (stride 1000), retrieving best-matching documents using TF-IDF on bigrams, and performing Smith-Waterman alignment (match score 2, insertion/deletion/substitution -1). For dev and test sets, human transcribers listened to audio while viewing transcripts and corrected 'clear and obvious' errors only to avoid introducing bias.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript (GT) and human rated transcript (HRT) was measured on dev/test sets, ranging from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere framework, Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss acoustic models, 4-gram KenLM language models, SVM with RBF kernel gender classifier, num2words library, pdftotext tool, custom HTML parsers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Pretrained models and training/decoding recipes are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/wav2letter.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender was labeled using an SVM gender classifier. Language is also collected as a dataset attribute.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors believe this dataset will promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and in multilingual ASR, and can also be used for Text-to-Speech (TTS) research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender classifier was trained primarily on LibriSpeech (English) data and applied to other languages. The dataset is based on read audiobooks from LibriVox, which may not be representative of all speech styles. Development and test sets were chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions by selecting speakers with high WER.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Polish has a high OOV rate of 13.39% which negatively impacts WER during LM decoding with constrained lexicon. The number replacement approach using pseudo labels is not perfect since pseudo labels may not always have correct transcription. The dataset only covers 8 languages with varying amounts of data (English dominates with 44.5K hours vs. ~100 hours for Polish).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation (development), and Testing for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Also suitable for Text-to-Speech (TTS) research and multilingual ASR research. Limited supervision subsets (10 hour, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets) are provided for low-resource training benchmarks.
